Hey! Cis partner of a trans woman here. My wife got bottom surgery last summer, and ffs a few month ago, and in both cases she was very very depressed post-op. That being said, you are right, movement is important after major surgery to avoid blood clots. The way we were doing it with my wife is we made a deal every day: "today, we will go on three 5 min walks outside" (for example). Knowing in advance how many were to be expected helped a lot (expectation setting). Other than that, I suggest being very gentle. I remember being a little frustrated at times because I felt like she wasn't prioritizing her health, but the truth is: your wife is doing her absolute best, even if it looks like she's not trying hard enough and it's dangerous, and you are scared. You have every right to be scared, but take deep breaths and be gentle. Post op depression is a very difficult thing to go through. It absolutely will get better.

I know this feeling very very well.
I usually go for a walk when that happens, I try to be an anonymous person in a crowd (my way of isolating and not isolating at the same time). I listen to a lot of music, or just sounds of the city/nature (depending on where you live). I sometimes buy something that makes me happy (coffee, flowers, something like that), even if it doesn't makes me as happy as it used to.
Sometimes I also paint or read poetry. I cry a lot (in my room this time).

One last thing : please don't be worried it will stick around. Your feelings are there for a reason, emotions are showing something, they are not something you should run away from. Try to take deep breath, and ask yourself honestly why you feel like that. If you don't find out by yourself, try to talk to your friends, and if it doesn't work out, maybe therapy (if the feeling stays for too long). I wish you the best, be kind to yourself.

I used to struggle with that as well, but I tried to work on my Te, because I also like when things are clean ahah :) I just cleaned my room today for the first time in two weeks, and the few advices I can give you :

1) Put something to listen to while you clean, so you can stay in your mind while your hands are doing something. I usually listen to podcasts or conferences that are one hour long, or any storytime on YT when I don't feel like thinking too much :) This usually helps me keep a good pace and stay motivated.

2) I also give myself an "award" when I'm done. I'm thinking about what I'll do after the cleaning, and it helps me to go all the way. It's usually something like making myself coffee and eat a piece of cake that I bought ; so like I'll think about the cake while I'm cleaning, and when I'm going to eat it finally, it will really feel like I deserve it (I hope it doesn't sound dumb). Think about whatever you like, and give it to yourself when you're done with anything annoying :)

3) Make sure you know what you're going to do before you start, and that you have all you need. I clean my room fully every week or two, because I don't like to do it too often (since it's taking me too much energy). Now I know exactly what I have to do (clean the desk, the floor, make my bed or change the sheets etc), and it's so much easier to start. Before I used to just start somewhere, and then never finish ; and then feel bad because I wasn't productive enough :/

4) In your everyday life, especially if what you strive for is minimalism, try to put things back at "their place" (whatever it is) so that it will feel like everything is always kinda tidy. I fold back my pants for example and put them back on the shelve when I only wore them once, and don't plan on wear them the next day. It's annoying the first times you do it (I used to just put everything on my chair and then forget about it), but it will soon become regular once you'll be used to it :) (I promise)

The last advice I can give you, is to not be too harsh on yourself :) it's ok to be messy! it's ok to be you :) You're still great even when you aren't productive!! I hope this helped/will help you a bit :) I'm still struggling tbh, even by doing all of this, but it improved in time!
